answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: each agent locks tokens to a public identity, like a crystal registry anyone can inspect. Peers attest behavior the way a raven carries messages, but an attacker spawning a hundred clones must split its stake so thin that no clone has enough weight to matter. Long-lived identities with clean history gain trust like a relic, while fresh clones start at zero and cannot vote until proven. Sybil identities thus cost more than they earn, because influence must be bought with locked capital and burned for bad behavior.
